newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong durian flights down as more goes by sea.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong durian flights down as more goes by sea.

text.p: The managing director of Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Ltd (HACTL), Anthony Charter, said increased shipments by sea of the seasonal fruit durian has weakened the perishable air import pattern.
At the height of the durian season in previous years up to 500 tonnes a day have been air freighted into the territory mainly from Thailand which hails the pungent delicacy as the 'king of fruit'.
"The amounts of durian being flown in is way below our forecast from what we would expect," Charter told Reuters in an interview.

"We are seeing a weaker perishable import pattern this year. Importers seem to have cracked the import of Durian by sea and use some sort of gas control system which slows down ripening so we are seeing smaller amounts of shipments by air which is affecting our May import figures,"
Cathay Pacific Cargo, which in previous years has arranged special Durian charter flights from Thailand to Hong Kong, said demand for flights this year was reduced.

"It is fair to say Thai exporters have not been beating down our door this year wanting flights. We have already arranged some flights but not as many as in the past. The market has been weaker," a Cathay source said.

Another factor was increased competition in the air cargo market from airlines such as Thai Airways International which operates a leased freighter into Hong Kong on an ad hoc basis, the Cathay source said.

"There are more carriers having a bite at the Durian market and there is more competition by sea either through faster journey times or they have dropped their rates. All that has had an effect and this year has not been the best," the source said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
